beats.say: Five Navy bombers flew out over the ocean on a training flight, and vanished off the radio.
beats.headline: CURSED OCEAN?
beats.short_title: Is the Bermuda Triangle Real? 🔍 Case #1
beats.comment: Would you sail through it? ⛵ yes / 🚫 no way
beats.bonus: Flight 19: on 5 December 1945 five US Navy TBM Avenger bombers on a training flight from Fort Lauderdale were lost with 14 airmen after their leader became disoriented; they most likely ran out of fuel over rough seas. A PBM Mariner search plane with 13 crew was also lost, most likely in an explosion. NOAA and the US Navy say the area sees no more losses than any other busy stretch of ocean; the name comes from a 1964 Argosy story by Vincent Gaddis.
beats.caption: Five bombers vanished in 1945. Meatball opened the Bermuda Triangle file.

Lightning hit the top of the Empire State Building. Then it hit it again.
beats.headline: STRIKES TWICE?
beats.short_title: Lightning Never Strikes Twice? WRONG ⚡ Case #6
beats.comment: Have you seen lightning hit something? ⚡ yes / 🙈 no
beats.bonus: NOAA's National Weather Service: lightning often strikes the same place repeatedly, especially tall, pointy, isolated objects; the Empire State Building is hit an average of 23 times a year. Park ranger Roy Sullivan was struck seven times between 1942 and 1977 and survived every one.
beats.caption: 'Lightning never strikes twice.' Meatball checked the weather records.

A farmer pulled the trigger on a pig, and two empires started loading cannons.
beats.headline: WAR OVER A PIG?
beats.short_title: The Pig War of 1859 Was REAL 🐷 Case #7
beats.comment: Would you go to war over a pig? 🐷 yes / 🙅 no way
beats.bonus: On San Juan Island in June 1859, American farmer Lyman Cutlar shot a Hudson's Bay Company pig that was eating his potatoes. He offered $10; the owner wanted $100. By August, 461 US soldiers with 14 cannons faced five Royal Navy warships with 70 guns and 2,140 men. Rear Admiral Robert Baynes refused to 'involve two great nations in a war over a squabble about a pig'. Nobody fired; the pig was the only casualty. In 1872 an arbitration by German Emperor Wilhelm I gave the islands to the US.
beats.caption: Two empires nearly went to war over one pig.

beats.headline: BAT BOMBS?
beats.short_title: The US Really Built BAT BOMBS 🦇 Case #9
beats.comment: Would you trust a bat with a bomb? 🦇 yes / 🙅 never
beats.bonus: Project X-Ray: in January 1942 dentist Lytle Adams proposed strapping small timed incendiaries to Mexican free-tailed bats, and President Roosevelt approved it. On 15 May 1943 armed bats escaped and set fire to the Carlsbad Army Airfield Auxiliary Air Base in New Mexico. The program was cancelled in 1944, after about $2 million, as the atomic bomb moved ahead.
beats.caption: The US military really built bat bombs, and the bats burned down its own air base.
